Lily Chang’s work on optimizing supply chain forecasting for a Fortune 500 client stands out. She led a team to refactor legacy models using PyTorch, achieving a 30% reduction in prediction error while maintaining real-time scalability. Her Python-based architecture decisions—such as modularizing data pipelines and mentoring junior engineers—enabled cross-team collaboration and minimized technical debt. When integrating third-party systems, she designed REST APIs that streamlined data ingestion, reducing manual intervention by 40%.  

As a professor, I’ve collaborated with Lily on two occasions, most recently during a research partnership with Veridio. Her ability to bridge academic rigor with industry pragmatism was evident in her work with Snowflake and dbt, where she automated complex SQL analytics workflows, cutting reporting latency by half. She consistently prioritizes clarity, whether explaining intricate PyTorch models to stakeholders or debugging production issues with her team.  

Lily’s strengths lie in her technical depth and collaborative mindset. She thrives in dynamic environments, as seen in her seamless use of Airflow to orchestrate end-to-end pipelines, ensuring reliability without compromising innovation. Her Python expertise extends beyond coding—she’s a strategic thinker who aligns technical solutions with business goals.  

In short, Lily is a rare blend of precision and adaptability. Her contributions to Veridio’s projects reflect both her technical mastery and her commitment to delivering impactful results. I’m confident she’ll excel in any role requiring data-driven leadership.
